ranking.rationale: Best owns Cratercade: Wish-specific kinetic machines, visible tracks and balances, and repeatable mechanical spectacle unite pinball skill with the bucket-to-flag jackpot.
Close fit for ingenious printed motion, explicit energy, accessible assembly, balance, capture, and reset; his single-input signature is narrower than this multi-control arcade.
Supports original replayable tabletop rules and mission variety, but personalized strategic games are less direct than kinetic craft for marble control and linked mechanisms.
Truthful physical cause and effect supports rolling and the weight-driven jackpot, but science teaching is secondary to the requested arcade experience.
Push and roll mechanics fit tactile launch and flipper control, but his compact motion toys are a narrower fit than the integrated tabletop arcade.
Reconfigurable printed pieces suit crater routes and mission layouts, while pattern arrangement does not own the launcher, flippers, and jackpot chain.
Engineering-honest mechanical models offer relevant craft, but Cratercade requires neither historic transport reconstruction nor a reference-based mechanised character.
Legible transformation relates to the raising flag, but deployment is one supporting event within a broader marble arcade.
Robust tactile printed assemblies are useful, but the requested generous arcade with multiple mechanisms is outside compact two- or three-part puzzles.
Captive paths loosely relate to ball retention, but loops, crossings, and topology do not create this pinball skill challenge or jackpot.
Hand-powered visual surprise is adjacent, but the lunar jackpot is a physical mechanical event rather than a light, aperture, or silhouette effect.
Mechanical story reveals are adjacent to the lunar flag event, but Cratercade has no shadow projection or hidden silhouette requirement.
Classic-game craft is only indirectly relevant: the Wish requests an original mechanical arcade rather than a personally adapted known tabletop classic.
Passive printed sound is not a required interaction; acoustic craft does not own the marble routes or bucket-to-flag mechanism.
Cinematic lunar form is supporting presentation, while no personal likeness reference is supplied and working arcade mechanisms lead the Wish.
Abstract strategic rules and combinatorial boards are far from the requested physical pinball skill, reconfigurable obstacles, and mechanical jackpot.
